evidence: Arithmetic (frozen bytes, template-identical test.sh/task.toml/env Dockerfile/restart_mcp.py by diff). Gates suite: render 600 + constraints 600 = 1200 s sequential (--max-concurrent-agent 1) < run_suite gates 1500 (test.sh:213). Scored suite: functional mode=individual, timeout 550 per criterion x 16 criteria = 8800 (rewardkit _arun_agent_individual runs criteria sequentially, judges.py:467-500) + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10600 s < run_suite scored 11100 (test.sh:224), margin 500 s. 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < [verifier].timeout_sec 13200 (task.toml:27), 600 s left for copy/launch/liveness/score.py. Liveness: startup probe 120 x 0.25 s (~30 s + probe time, test.sh:115-125); restart helper 5 s kill wait + 30 s readiness < restart_mcp HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC 55 (restart_mcp.py:11). Agent 7200 s and build 600 s are template values; agent image is template-identical (node slim + express/better-sqlite3), hosted env setup 2-18 s, hosted v2 agent finished in ~8 min. Adequacy: the functional comment itself says 'Not yet measured against a judge run' and the raw evidence index has no judge-duration measurement for these bytes. Indirect evidence: two hosted runs on 9 Oct of v2 (same 550 s individual config, same 16 criterion ids, same GLM judge) completed with no 'judge timed out' errors in any of 32 functional sessions; verifier wall time 63 min (oracle) and 76 min (agent), restart (inside last functional criterion) at ~54/67 min, i.e. avg <=~200-240 s per session including image build. But v3 enlarged several functional criteria (words: wall_every_route 184->337, wall_mentions_and_links 166->331, edits_and_stale_edit 200->372, search_and_transcript 205->343, timer_changes 243->330) and replaced polish with 6 interactive criteria in one batched 900 s session; these were not timed. A rewardkit timeout records the criterion as 0.0 (judges.py:285-303, 545-549), so a conforming app could lose a whole weight-4.0 criterion if the GLM judge overruns 550 s on the heaviest legs. Also harness-level: schema-mismatch retries (_MAX_JUDGE_RETRIES=3) can each consume a full timeout, which the nominal sum does not cover (template property, not task-specific). Nesting holds; length adequacy for current bytes is unmeasured, hence risk=true.
suggested_fix: No byte change required for nesting. Before packaging, obtain a full configured judge run of the current bytes (oracle) and record per-criterion durations of the heaviest functional criteria (wall_every_route, wall_mentions_and_links, edits_and_stale_edit, search_and_transcript) and the 6-criterion polish session; if any approaches 550/900 s or times out, split or trim those legs rather than raising budgets automatically.
